critical_evidence.evidence: The dealer text says 'fully serviced including timing belt, water pump'. There is no invoice, date, mileage or parts list. At 155k the car is between the 90k and 180k intervals, and an original-belt history is possible without proof.

The claimed OME 2-inch full suspension and Dobinsons UCAs are quality brands, not a spacer lift. No invoice or alignment printout. Rear air-bag retention versus coil conversion and height-control light status are unstated. Photo 1 (probable match) shows a level stance only.
No underside photos or inspection. The car is in San Diego, but where it lived before is unknown. Rock sliders and the bumper can hide frame and rocker condition.
No dash photo with ignition on and no statement on CEL, VSC or height-control lights.
The listing claims four Falken Wildpeak tires on four Method wheels. Photo 1 shows matching all-terrains on the visible corners of a probably matching white GX. DOT date codes are unknown.

The radiator (OEM plastic-tank failure point) is not mentioned. There is no leak statement. The water pump is claimed replaced without receipt. The rack-and-pinion replacement is claimed, and its cause (leak?) is unknown.

documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present. The VIN decodes consistently, the price is stated as including dealer fees, and a history summary reports no accident or damage. The maintenance half is missing. The timing belt, water pump, rack, CVs and control arms are dealer claims with no receipts, dates or mileages, and there are no underside photos.

condition.rationale: Nothing wrong is stated, and a long list of fresh parts is claimed but unproven. No verifiable evidence establishes rust status, radiator, warning lights or tire dates. The heavy trail hardware could signal use.

price_value.rationale: The $25,995 asking price is well above the $12,983–$20,339 fair-value range. It is also above the 2006 Base active peer ($24,995 with 8k fewer miles) and in line with this dealer's own priced builds. Much of the premium is off-road hardware the capability intent says is not worth paying for.

mission_fit.rationale: A body-on-frame V8 4WD with a Prinsu platform rack delivers the rooftop-tent and camping capability the RX 350 lacks, so it fits the utility branch. The winch bumper, sliders and light bar exceed the stated intent. The price sits at the top of the budget band rather than decisively inside it.

logistics.rationale: California dealer in San Diego, roughly a flight plus a one-day drive to Carmel. CA registration and smog are straightforward through a CA dealer. PPI access is plausible locally but not confirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: The 2009 final year in white over grey is mildly desirable. The buyer favours stock or mostly stock, though, and this is a full dealer overland build. The parts are quality brands, not cheap, so it nets out to a typical-to-mixed example.

positives: The VIN is disclosed and decodes as a 2009 GX 470 4.7L V8, matching the ad with no identity conflicts.
The history summary shows no accident or damage reported, and the price is stated as including all dealer fees.
An extensive claimed service list includes timing belt, water pump, brakes and rotors, CV axles, rack and pinion, lower control arms and rear diff service. It is valuable if receipts exist.
The lift is quality-brand (OME, Dobinsons) rather than a spacer or cheap kit.
The Prinsu roof rack directly suits the rooftop-tent camping intent.
It is a Southern California dealer car, a lower rust-exposure location (inferred; prior history unknown).
concerns: Observed: the asking price of $25,995 is well above the fair-value estimate of $12,983–$20,339. The premium is largely off-road accessories that add little value under the stated capability intent.

Observed: the heavy trail hardware (DV8 winch bumper, rock sliders, light bar) adds front weight and can signal hard off-road use. Front-end replacements (rack, CV axles, lower arms) suggest significant wear was present before the build.

ppi_focus: Verify timing belt and water pump work: belt date sticker, fresh components, and no weep at the water pump or thermostat housing
Radiator tanks and seams for seepage; cooling system pressure test
Rear suspension configuration, height-control/VSC codes, and full-system scan including SAI pump and valves
Frame, crossmembers and rockers behind the DV8 sliders for rust, dents or trail damage; skid plates and bumper mounts for impact marks
Front end with the OME/Dobinsons parts: ball joints, CV boot condition, UCA bushings, steering rack for leaks, and the alignment printout
Exhaust manifolds for cracks or tick on cold start
Transmission, transfer case and differential fluid condition; driveline vibration at speed with the lift
Tire date codes, even wear, and proper wheel offset and clearance
Dashboard for cracks; check for KDSS and, if present, its cylinder and lines
Wiring quality for the light bar, fogs and any winch (fusing, relays, no chafing)
what_would_change_verdict: Dated invoices for the timing belt, water pump, rack and the suspension build would lift documentation and condition substantially.
A clean independent PPI with a dry underside, no rust, sound radiator and no codes would raise condition.
A meaningful price reduction toward the fair-value range would improve price_value.
Down: evidence of hard trail use (frame or skid damage), a failing radiator, rust behind the sliders, stored codes, or refusal of records or PPI.
evidence.mission_note: A GX470 with a platform rack genuinely adds rooftop-tent and body-on-frame 4WD capability the RX 350 lacks, which is the only justification for this branch. This build carries far more off-road hardware than the camping intent needs, and it is priced for that hardware.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2009 GX 470 4.7L V8 consistent with the ad, and a history summary reports no accident or damage with multiple owners. Nothing mechanical is stated as wrong, but every service item is a dealer claim with no receipt, date or mileage. That includes the timing belt and water pump, the profile's key price driver. The rear suspension configuration, radiator, frame condition, warning lights and tire dates are all unaddressed. The car is a full dealer overland build (OME lift, winch bumper, sliders, light bar), which exceeds the stated capability intent. The front-end replacements (rack, CVs, lower arms) indicate significant prior wear of unknown cause. At $25,995 it sits well above the $12,983–$20,339 fair-value range. The attached photos include several other dealer vehicles, so only photo 1 appears to show this car.
evidence.next_action: Ask the seller: Can you send the invoice for the timing belt and water pump showing date, mileage, and whether the idler, tensioner, thermostat and cam/crank seals were replaced?
